definitions.explanation: The master or owner of a house, establishment, or domain. Carries a traditional, slightly formal or literary tone.
The person who receives and entertains guests. Used in traditional or formal contexts.

examples.japanese: この{城|しろ}の{主|あるじ}は{誰|だれ}だ。
examples.english: Who is the lord of this castle?

examples.japanese: {店|みせ}の{主|あるじ}が{自|みずか}ら{料理|りょうり}を{運|はこ}んできた。
examples.english: The shop owner personally brought the food.

examples.japanese: {主|あるじ}のいない{屋敷|やしき}は、{長年|ながねん}の{間|あいだ}{荒|あ}れ{放題|ほうだい}だった。
examples.english: The mansion without its master had been left to ruin for years.

examples.japanese: {宴|うたげ}の{主|あるじ}が{客|きゃく}を{迎|むか}えた。
examples.english: The host of the banquet greeted the guests.

examples.japanese: {主|あるじ}として{客人|きゃくじん}をもてなす。
examples.english: To entertain guests as the host.

examples.japanese: {茶会|ちゃかい}の{主|あるじ}は、{一|ひと}つ{一|ひと}つの{道具|どうぐ}に{心|こころ}を{込|こ}めて{準備|じゅんび}した。
examples.english: The host of the tea ceremony prepared each utensil with care.

notes:
A slightly literary or traditional word for 'master' or 'owner.' More formal and evocative than {主人|しゅじん}, often used in storytelling, historical contexts, and descriptions of traditional settings.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {城|しろ}の{主|あるじ} — lord of a castle
- {店|みせ}の{主|あるじ} — shop owner/proprietor
- {屋敷|やしき}の{主|あるじ} — master of the mansion
- {宴|うたげ}の{主|あるじ} — host of a feast
- {主|あるじ}のいない — without its master/owner

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {主人|しゅじん} — master; husband; proprietor (more common in everyday speech)
- {持|も}ち{主|ぬし} — owner (of an object)
- {飼|か}い{主|ぬし} — pet owner
- {家主|やぬし} — landlord

NOTE ON READINGS:
The kanji {主|あるじ} has several readings: あるじ (master/host — this entry), ぬし (owner, often in compounds like {持|も}ち{主|ぬし}), and しゅ (on'yomi, in compounds like {主人|しゅじん}).
